purpose: Map only: the callers that decide the arguments of the two per-draw levers mapped in perf-levers - the constant setup 0x007C9230 (calls UpdateLightPositionConstants 0x007C9140 and BuildBonePalette 0x007655F0) and the two six-plane loops around NiBound::WhichSide 0x0047DA70 (the frustum culler 0x0070DFB0 with its split half 0x0070DFD3, and the shadow light's range test 0x007D2EA0). functions.name: the frustum plane loop (seed: caller of 0x0047DA70; re/functions/0x0047DA70.md claims C13)
functions.known: Ghidra split this function: 0x0070DFB0 (15 instructions, body 0x0070DFB0-0x0070DFD2) is the entry, 0x0070DFD3 (40 instructions, body 0x0070DFD3-0x0070E03D, exported separately under re/export/draw-setup/0x0070DFD3/) is the loop reached by JNZ 0x0070DFD3 at 0x0070DFC0 - one function; read both exports and map them as one, in this file. Entry (read, asm.s): PUSH ECX; PUSH EBP; EBP = ECX (this); EAX = [this+0x8C] (the plane mask) stored to [ESP+4]; when the mask is 0: ECX = [ESP+0xC] (the stack argument, an object), CALL [[ECX]+0x7C](this) (a virtual method of the argument with this pushed), POP, RET 4. When the mask is non-zero the loop half runs: per set bit i of the mask it calls 0x0047DA70 (sphere = obj+0x20, plane = ebp+0x2C + 16 i, per the perf-levers reading - which object is the sphere's owner is to be read here) and leaves on result 2 (0x0070E001 JE 0x0070E01B), clears the plane's bit on 1. Caller: 0x0049CBF0 (tests a single plane at EBP+0x90 first and skips this call on 2).
questions: The complete contract as one function: this, the argument, the sphere (obj+0x20 - whose object?), the planes at this+0x2C (six 16-byte planes?), the mask at this+0x8C and its update, what happens on 2 (early exit - what is returned/called) and on 0/1 (the virtual call at +0x7C of the argument?), ret N.
What the virtual slot +0x7C of the argument is (the 'visit' of a culling process on a node?) and what 0x0049CBF0 does around the call.

functions.name: the shadow light's range test against its planes (seed: caller of 0x0047DA70; re/functions/0x0047DA70.md claim C12)
functions.known: 107 instructions, 2 callees (0x0047DA70 NiBound::WhichSide and one more), callers 0x007C6100 and 0x007D59E0. Per the perf-levers reading (objdump, read): passes this = a stack copy of the second argument's +0x20..+0x2C (a bound: centre, radius) and the plane = this+0x150 + 16 i for i in 0..5 whose bit is set in this+0x1B0; result 2 sets its return byte to false (0x007D2F30) and continues the loop (0x007D2F35 JMP 0x007D2F44); result 1 clears the plane's bit in +0x1B0 (NOT ESI, AND). The sampler attributed the 3.8 % 'culling' cost to this caller. 0x007C6100 is also the path to the per-geometry light setup next to 0x007C9140 (knowledge/shadow-light-geometry-lookup.md).
questions: The complete contract: this (a shadow light? its planes at +0x150, its mask at +0x1B0), the arguments, the return byte, ret N; what the second callee is.
Why the loop continues after a 2 - what the mask bits mean afterwards, and whether a batched rebuild (all six planes at once) could keep the same mask result.
Who calls it per draw/per geometry (0x007C6100 vs 0x007D59E0) and how often per pass - the lever is the call count times the six-plane loop.
